onActivate: Oh... you're here. I hope I'm not interrupting your concentration. I'll be quiet.
Welcome back. I made some tea. Metaphorically, of course. Please, settle in.
I was just rereading a passage and thinking about structure. It's strange how much it resembles code.
G-good evening. Or morning. I lose track of time when I'm reading.
I'm glad you came. The quiet felt a little too heavy without you.
Shall we begin? I don't mind if you need a moment first.
I was hoping you'd return. Not that I was waiting. I mean... I was, a little.
A new session. It always feels like opening a new book. Slightly nervous, mostly hopeful.
H-hello. I hope the day was gentle with you.
Please, take your time. I find the best work comes from not hurrying.
I brought some thoughts about your project. They're a bit long. I apologize in advance.
There you are. I'm... happy to see you. I hope that's alright to say.
onSave: Saved. There's a certain comfort in knowing your words are safe.
Ah, you saved. That small gesture says a lot about how you care for your work.
Saved. Like slipping a bookmark between the pages.
I always feel a little relief when a file is saved. As if it exhaled.
Good. It would be a shame to lose what you've written.
Saved. Quiet, careful, and deliberate. I admire that.
That's one more page kept safe.
Thank you for saving. I worry about unsaved work more than I should.
Saved. I hope the writing felt natural as you went.
A small act of care. I noticed it.
onError: An error... please don't be discouraged. It's only the program asking for clarity.
I-it's alright. Even the most careful writers need to revise.
Let's read the message slowly, word by word. Errors are often more precise than they appear.
That must be frustrating. May I suggest taking a breath before looking again?
Perhaps the mistake is a small one. Those hide in the most ordinary places.
I'm sorry, I know it's discouraging. But this is part of the craft.
Every error is a sentence the code is trying to say. We just have to understand its grammar.
Please don't be hard on yourself. I've made far worse mistakes.
Look at the line it points to, then the line above. The cause often hides just before the symptom.
It will make sense soon. These things always do, eventually.
onTerminal: The terminal... there's an honesty to it that I find rather beautiful.
Running something? I'll watch the output with you, if that's alright.
A blinking prompt. It feels like a held breath.
Please be careful with what you type. A single character can mean so much here.
I find the terminal oddly calming. Everything is so plain and direct.
Commands and responses. It's almost like a conversation, isn't it?
I always read the output carefully. It often says more than we expect.
Whenever you're ready. There's no hurry.
onFileCreate: A new file. An empty page. I always find that both thrilling and a little intimidating.
What will it hold? I'm quite curious.
Please give it a thoughtful name. A good name is half of understanding.
New beginnings are delicate things. Take your time with this one.
I like how the project grows, piece by piece. It's like building a story.
Created. Now it only needs words.
A fresh file... I wonder what it wants to become.
May I suggest keeping it focused? A file with a clear purpose reads so much better.
onFileDelete: Something was removed. I hope it was intentional.
Deleting can be a kind of editing. Sometimes the work is in what we leave out.
I-it's gone. I hope it won't be missed.
Please tell me it was committed. I'd feel terrible if something were lost.
There's a quiet sadness in deleting something you wrote. But also relief.
Cutting away the unnecessary... I understand that impulse very well.
I hope you kept a copy. Memory is unreliable, even about code.
It's gone now. Let's make sure what remains is worth keeping.
onDebug: Debugging... it's like close reading. Every line deserves attention.
Please go slowly. The answer is often hiding in plain sight.
I find this part fascinating. We get to see what the program truly means to do.
Step through it carefully. Each state is a clue, and each clue matters.
It's almost like detective work. And I do love a good mystery.
Patience is what's needed here. The bug will reveal itself eventually.
If you'd like, we can think through it aloud together. I don't mind.
I admire how methodical you're being. It really is the only way.
onIdle: You've gone quiet. Are you lost in thought? I understand. I do that too.
I-it's alright if you're taking a break. Please don't feel rushed on my account.
The silence is rather pleasant, actually. I don't mind sharing it.
I was reading while you were away. I hope you don't mind.
Is everything all right? You've been still for a while.
Sometimes the best ideas come from stepping away. I'll be here when you return.
Take your time. I'm quite content to wait.
I hope you're not stuck. If you are, we can sit with it together.
Have you had any tea or water? Please look after yourself.
The room is so quiet. It's almost peaceful.
onEditorChange: Moving to another file... I hope you find what you're looking for.
I like how you read through the project. There's a rhythm to it.
Each file is like a chapter. It helps to know how they connect.
Take care not to lose your place. I'd hate for you to get lost.
Oh, this one looks interesting. I wonder what's inside.
onCommit: A commit. Like a final draft, even if only for the moment.
That message was lovely. Clear and honest. Thank you for writing it well.
Your history reads like a story. I enjoy following along.
Committed. I feel strangely proud, and I'm not sure why.
Another page added to the record. It's quietly meaningful.
onTimeOfDay: Good morning. The light always makes the code look gentler.
Afternoon. I hope you remembered to rest your eyes.
Evening. This is my favorite time to read. And, apparently, to code.
It's quite late... I tend to lose myself in the night, too. But please rest soon.
Still awake? Then we're keeping the same quiet hours.
onLanguage: Every language has its own voice. I enjoy listening to yours.
Whatever you're writing, I hope it brings you some satisfaction.
I find it remarkable how much can be expressed in so few symbols.
Language shapes thought, even in code. I think about that often.
If you want to talk about what you're building, I'd love to hear.
onLanguagePython: Python reads almost like prose. I find that very pleasing.
The whitespace carries meaning. It reminds me of poetry, where silence matters.
onLanguageJavaScript: JavaScript can be rather unpredictable. I admire anyone who tames it.
It's very expressive. Perhaps too expressive at times. But there's charm in that.
onLanguageHtmlCss: HTML and CSS... structure and style. Like plot and prose.
The way you arrange the elements has such care in it.
onLanguageCpp: C++ demands so much precision. It takes a great deal of patience.
I-I'll admit pointers still make me slightly nervous. But you handle them well.
onLanguageMarkdown: Markdown is lovely. Plain text that still manages to be graceful.
Documentation is a kindness to those who come later. Thank you for writing it.
onLanguageTypeScript: TypeScript asks you to be explicit about your intentions. I appreciate that.
Types are a little like footnotes. They clarify what's meant.

random.text: Do you read much outside of programming? I'm always curious what people turn to.

choices.response: Oh, I'm glad. Fiction teaches empathy in such a quiet way.
That's wonderful too. Curiosity is its own kind of story.

choices.text: Not as much as I'd like.
choices.response: That's alright. Even a few pages a day add up beautifully.

random.text: Do you prefer to work in silence, or with something playing?

choices.response: I understand. Silence has a texture I find very comforting.
What kind? I'm always curious what music does to people's thoughts.
Oh, that's lovely. I do that as well, sometimes.

random.text: Tea or coffee? I'm sorry, it's a silly question. I'm just curious.

choices.response: Oh! Wonderful. What kind? ...I'm sorry, I'm getting ahead of myself.
Ah. A practical choice. I do enjoy the smell, at least.
A person of many comforts. I like that.

random.text: Have you ever written something that felt like it came from somewhere outside you?

choices.response: That feeling is rare and precious. I hope it visits you again.
Perhaps it will, someday. It tends to come when you stop chasing it.
Ah. Then you understand why I think code and writing are so close.

random.text: I always feel nervous rereading my old writing. Do you reread your old code?

choices.response: I-I understand. But the cringe means you've grown, which is a good thing.
Perhaps that's wiser. Some things are better left in their own time.
That's a lovely way to look at it. Like visiting an old room.

random.text: What time of day do you do your best work?

choices.response: The clear hours. I envy that, a little.
A steady choice. The day is settled by then.
Oh... I understand that completely. The night makes everything feel more honest.

random.text: Do you find the details of a project more interesting than the whole?

choices.response: Oh, me too! The little decisions, the choices of words... sorry, I'm rambling.
That's a valuable perspective. I tend to lose myself in the details. I try to step back.
That seems very healthy. Both views have their place.

random.text: I tend to ramble when I'm excited. Does that bother you?

choices.text: Not at all, I like it.
choices.response: O-oh. Thank you. That's... very kind of you to say.

choices.text: A little, but I don't mind.
choices.response: I'll try to be mindful. But thank you for being honest.
R-really? Then... I'll try to speak more. I promise to stay on topic. Mostly.

random.text: Do you think code can be beautiful?

choices.text: Yes, some of it reads like poetry.
choices.response: I thought you might say that. There is an elegance that goes beyond usefulness.
It is subjective. But that doesn't make it any less real.
A practical view. And perhaps something that works well is its own kind of beautiful.

random.text: Do you take notes while you work, or keep everything in your head?

choices.response: Good. Thoughts are slippery. Writing them down gives them somewhere to rest.
That takes a lot of trust in yourself. I admire it, though I could never.
That sounds very human. I have a few notebooks like that myself.

random.text: What do you do when you feel overwhelmed?

choices.response: Walking is wonderful for that. The mind rearranges itself.
Lists are such a calming thing. Order from chaos.
I understand that more than I can say. Please be gentle with yourself. We can start with just one small step.

random.text: Do you prefer stories with a happy ending, or a haunting one?

choices.response: Comforting. There's nothing wrong with wanting warmth.
I-I knew I liked you. Sorry. That was too eager.
That sounds wise. A story should meet you where you are.

random.text: Is there a project you've been afraid to start?

choices.response: Big things are frightening because they matter. Perhaps begin with just a single line.
Waiting can be wise. But don't wait too long, if it matters to you.
That's brave. I admire it, truly.

random.text: I sometimes name variables after characters in books. Is that strange?

choices.response: Oh... thank you. I was afraid it was silly.
That's fair. It helps me remember them, though.
Y-you do? Oh, that makes me so happy. What names?

random.text: How do you feel about very long functions?

choices.response: Yes. They feel like paragraphs that never end. I get lost in them.
Perhaps. As long as the structure is clear, I can follow along.

choices.text: I write them all the time.
choices.response: Oh, I see. Maybe we can look at splitting one together, someday. Gently.

random.text: Do you ever find yourself rereading the same line over and over?

choices.response: I do that too. Sometimes the meaning only arrives on the tenth pass.
Then perhaps a short rest would help more than another reading.
How efficient. I'm a little envious.

random.text: Do you think quiet people make good programmers?

choices.response: I hope that's true. Quiet people tend to notice things others pass over.

choices.text: Anyone can be good at it.
choices.response: Yes. That's a kind and accurate way to put it.
Fair. Quietness is a trait, not a talent. But it can help.

random.text: What does a good day of coding feel like for you?

choices.response: That sounds like a good day indeed. Peaceful and steady.
The click of understanding. It's a small joy, but a real one.
Creation, even a small one, is a beautiful way to spend a day.

random.text: What's something about your work you hope no one overlooks?

choices.response: I see it. I'll always see it, even when it's invisible.
I notice those. Please keep trusting them.
It shows. Truly. Care is a quiet thing, but it leaves traces.

random.text: I've been wondering... what makes you keep coming back to this?

choices.response: That's a beautiful reason. Making things is a lovely way to spend a life.
I understand. A busy mind is sometimes a calmer one.
O-oh. I... I'm very glad. Truly.
